questions.question:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusion logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

No photographer is an architect.

All engineers are photographers.

All postmen are architects.

**Conclusions:**

I. No engineer is an architect.

II. No engineer is a postman.

III. No photographer is a postman.

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

Concept:

1) We have to check the conclusions are 100% match with the statement. If the conclusion is 100% match with the given statement then the conclusion is true. If there is a 1% chance of not following the statement then the conclusion is considered to be false.

2) The possibility case can be considered to be "false" in "definite case".

3) In Possibility case, either "can" or "possible" word must be present.

__Explanation__

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5635a53e4097205b8989a36fc9227e5275207b8bbad5d20afc8dfee8d91777ef.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. No engineer is an architect. → True (Since all engineers are photographers and no photographer is an architect, no engineer can be architect.)

II. No engineer is a postman. → True(Since all engineers are photographers and all postmen are architect and no photographer is an architect, no engineer can be a postman.)

III. No photographer is a postman. → True (Since all postmen are architect and no architect is photographer, no photographer can be a postman.)

Hence, the correct answer is **"All conclusions follow"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question: In a code language, if RELATED is written as 72, then how will FRANCE be written in the same language?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/88cbd8fdbc15586c25020abd305dd0547df7be194a0223742d1e9a165ba86a30.png] 

The logic follows here is :

**(Sum of place values of alphabets in the word) + (Number of alphabets in that word) = Given code.**

For RELATED = 72

Number of alphabets = 7

(18 + 5 + 12 + 1 + 20 + 5 + 4) + 7 = 65 + 7 = 72.

Similarly,

**For FRANCE**

**Number of alphabets = 6**

**(6 + 18 + 1 + 14 + 3 + 5) + 6 = 47 + 6 = 53.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"53".**

questions.question:
Select the options that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number. 

14 : 238 :: 22 : ?
questions.solution:
The logic follows here is :

**Second number = (First number) × (First number + 3).**

For 14 : 238

14 × (14 + 3) = 14 × 17 = 238.

Similarly,

**For 22 : ?**

**? = 22 × (22 + 3) = 22 × 25 = 550.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"550".**

questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All nurses are gods.

Some nurses are doctors.

Conclusions:

I. Some gods are nurses.

II. Some doctors are gods.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as below,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a731d4cd82ee5d3a108c8159fab0a9a596b04bf906e84bbb0a33710be9848c54.png] 

**Conclusions:** 

1. Some gods are nurses → True (As all the nurses are god is a definite conclusion then some gods are nurses will also be a definite conclusion).

2. Some doctors are gods → True (As all the nurses are gods is a definite conclusion and some of the doctors are nurses then, the doctor which are nurses will also be a god is a definite conclusion).

Hence, the correct answer is "**Both** **conclusions I and II follow".**
